key_insight: ARGON speeds up neutral-atom compilation by decoupling static spatial conflict resolution from temporal routing and using a GNN to choose layouts that avoid future bottlenecks.
engineering_relevance: It makes large-scale neutral atom programs more practical by improving compilation scalability, reducing transport-induced decoherence, and preserving high parallelism under strict hardware constraints.
method: Offline precompute a library of hardware-certified, high-parallelism spatial layouts.
Use a GNN to score candidate layouts against long-horizon temporal effects and avoid downstream routing conflicts.
Apply a heuristic router to convert the chosen layout sequence into collision-free atom transport.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports compilation in under 10 seconds, up to >10^4x speedup over the best baselines, and up to 10^2x fidelity improvement on dense circuits.
watch_item: The approach depends on the quality of offline-certified layouts and GNN predictions, so generalization to new hardware constraints or circuit patterns may require retraining or library updates.
paper_title: ARGON: A GNN-Empowered Compilation Framework for Scalable Neutral Atom Computing
